document.title: ICC Return to Play Post Pregnancy Guidelines

scope.summary: A general framework for science and medicine staff and ICC Member boards to support return to play after pregnancy.
limitations: The framework must be applied subject to relevant local legislation and regulations.
The document does not define camera-test pass thresholds.
The document does not provide a complete automated medical-clearance algorithm.

careTeam.caseManager: A doctor or physiotherapist is usually identified as the primary point of contact.

managementReviews.note: Announcement remains at the player's discretion.
Continues once the player decides to reintegrate into the cricket environment.

managementReviewsReference.section: How to approach return to play for the cricket player

stages.label: Ready
guidance: Begin early pelvic floor activation under appropriate guidance.
Support psychological adjustment to life as a mother.
Gradually increase exercise tolerance, beginning with gentle walking and progressing as able under medical-team guidance.

stages.label: Review
stages.purpose: Coordinate external and internal health, wellbeing, and practical reviews.
guidance: Obtain an obstetrician or general-practitioner review and clearance, including wound review.
Arrange a pelvic floor assessment with a Women's Health Physiotherapist.
Review bloods, including iron, with the cricket doctor.
Address relevant musculoskeletal issues with the physiotherapist.
Begin a graduated introduction to strength training with the Strength and Conditioning Coach.
Review psychological stressors, including possible birth trauma.
Review energy availability and practical nutrition needs, particularly when breastfeeding.
Consider childcare, social support, and feeding or pumping facilities.
Introduce comfortable non-ballistic aerobic activity and graded strength training.
Review sports-bra fit.

stages.label: Restore
stages.purpose: Prepare for return to a structured training environment.
guidance: Use a graduated return-to-run program developed with Women's Health Physiotherapy and the medical and performance team.
Establish social supports and training flexibility.
Recognise and address fatigue, recovery, childcare, mental-health, and physical barriers to return.

stages.label: Recondition
stages.purpose: Build toward sport-specific training load and a sustained return to play.
guidance: Use reconditioning and graded exposure toward a sport-specific training load.
Account for time away from training and musculoskeletal overuse-injury risks in programming.

stages.label: Return
guidance: The player returns to play.

stages.label: Refine
stages.purpose: Continue monitoring and adapt practical support.
guidance: Continue reviewing social support and practical training and travel requirements.
Monitor musculoskeletal and pelvic floor symptoms.
Use a whole-system approach to sleep, recovery, and low energy availability.
